report.headline: Part 1 and Part 2 need the most work.
report.summary: The answer correctly explains how wetlands hold stormwater and identifies useful maintenance actions like desilting and community monitoring. However, the claim regarding an 80% reduction in every city is exaggerated, and the suggestion to concrete wetland beds contradicts the goal of conservation. You should first replace the concreting suggestion with measures that maintain natural soil permeability and vegetation.
report.question: Discuss how urban wetlands reduce flood risk and suggest ways to conserve them.

directives.meaning: Look at the issue from more than one side, with reasons, and reach a balanced view.
Propose practical measures and say who should act and how.

sentences.text: Urban wetlands hold stormwater after heavy rain, so less water enters drains at once.
This is why wetland restoration has reduced flooding by 80% in every Indian city where it has been attempted.
Municipalities should concrete all wetland beds to stop seepage, build retaining walls and prohibit any human entry.
Regular desilting and community monitoring can help protect the area.
These measures will end urban floods.
